questions.text: Let $[\cdot]$ denote the greatest integer function. If the domain of the function $f(x)=\cos^{-1}\left(\dfrac{4x+2[x]}{3}\right)$ is $[\alpha,\beta]$, then $12(\alpha+\beta)$ is equal to:
questions.sol:
Need $-3\le 4x+2[x]\le 3$. Write $x=n+f$, $n=[x]$, $0\le f<1$: $-3\le 6n+4f\le 3$.
$n=0$: $0\le 4f\le 3 \Rightarrow x\in\left[0,\dfrac34\right]$.
$n=-1$: $-3\le -6+4f \Rightarrow f\ge\dfrac34 \Rightarrow x\in\left[-\dfrac14,0\right)$.
Other $n$ give no solutions, so the domain is $\left[-\dfrac14,\dfrac34\right]$.
$12(\alpha+\beta)=12\cdot\dfrac12=6$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: If the set of all solutions of $|x^2+x-9|=|x|+|x^2-9|$ is $[\alpha,\beta]\cup[\gamma,\infty)$, then $(\alpha^2+\beta^2+\gamma^2)$ is equal to:
questions.sol:
$x^2+x-9 = x+(x^2-9)$, and $|a+b|=|a|+|b|$ holds exactly when $ab\ge 0$.
So we need $x(x^2-9)\ge 0 \iff x(x-3)(x+3)\ge0 \iff x\in[-3,0]\cup[3,\infty)$.
$\alpha=-3,\ \beta=0,\ \gamma=3$, so $\alpha^2+\beta^2+\gamma^2=9+0+9=18$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: Let $z$ be a complex number such that $|z+2|=|z-2|$ and $\arg\left(\dfrac{z+3}{z-i}\right)=\dfrac{\pi}{4}$. Then $|z|^2$ is equal to:
questions.sol:
$|z+2|=|z-2|$ means $z$ lies on the perpendicular bisector of $-2$ and $2$, the imaginary axis: $z=iy$.
$\dfrac{z+3}{z-i}=\dfrac{3+iy}{i(y-1)}=\dfrac{(3+iy)(-i)}{y-1}=\dfrac{y-3i}{y-1}$.
Argument $\dfrac{\pi}{4}$: real part $=$ imaginary part $>0$, so $\dfrac{y}{y-1}=\dfrac{-3}{y-1} \Rightarrow y=-3$ (then both parts equal $\dfrac34>0$).
$z=-3i$, so $|z|^2=9$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: The number of functions $f:\{1,2,3,4\}\to\{a,b,c\}$, which are not onto, is:
questions.sol:
Total functions: $3^4=81$.
Onto functions: $3^4-\binom31 2^4+\binom32 1^4=81-48+3=36$.
Not onto: $81-36=45$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: Let $$S=\left\{A=\begin{bmatrix} a & b\\ c & d\end{bmatrix} : a,b,c,d\in\{0,1,2,3,4\} \text{ and } A^2-4A+3I=0\right\}$$ be a set of $2\times2$ matrices. Then the number of matrices in $S$, for which the sum of the diagonal elements is equal to $4$, is:
questions.sol:
By the Cayley–Hamilton theorem, $A^2-(\operatorname{tr}A)A+(\det A)I=0$.
With $\operatorname{tr}A=a+d=4$: $A^2-4A+3I=(3-\det A)I$, so we need $\det A=ad-bc=3$.
$(a,d)=(0,4),(4,0)$: $bc=-3$, impossible.
$(a,d)=(1,3),(3,1)$: $bc=0$, which has $5+5-1=9$ choices of $(b,c)$ each, giving $18$.
$(a,d)=(2,2)$: $bc=1 \Rightarrow b=c=1$, giving $1$.
Total $=19$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: Let $A=\begin{bmatrix}1&1&2\\-2&0&1\\1&3&5\end{bmatrix}$. Then the sum of all elements of the matrix $\operatorname{adj}\left(\operatorname{adj}\left(2(\operatorname{adj}A)^{-1}\right)\right)$ is equal to:
questions.sol:
$|A|=1(0-3)-1(-10-1)+2(-6-0)=-3+11-12=-4$.
$(\operatorname{adj}A)^{-1}=\dfrac{A}{|A|}=-\dfrac{A}{4}$, so $B=2(\operatorname{adj}A)^{-1}=-\dfrac{A}{2}$.
For a $3\times3$ matrix, $\operatorname{adj}(\operatorname{adj}B)=|B|\,B$, and $|B|=\left(-\dfrac12\right)^3(-4)=\dfrac12$.
So $\operatorname{adj}(\operatorname{adj}B)=\dfrac12\left(-\dfrac A2\right)=-\dfrac A4$.
Sum of elements of $A$ $=1+1+2-2+0+1+1+3+5=12$, so the required sum is $-\dfrac{12}{4}=-3$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: The first term of an A.P. of $30$ non-negative terms is $\dfrac{10}{3}$. If the sum of this A.P. is the cube of its last term, then its common difference is:
questions.sol:
Let $l=a+29d$ be the last term. $S_{30}=15(a+l)=l^3$.
With $a=\dfrac{10}{3}$: $15\left(\dfrac{10}{3}+l\right)=l^3 \Rightarrow l^3-15l-50=0 \Rightarrow (l-5)(l^2+5l+10)=0$.
So $l=5$ (the quadratic has no real root).
$29d=5-\dfrac{10}{3}=\dfrac53 \Rightarrow d=\dfrac{5}{87}$.

questions.text: The number of ways, of forming a queue of $4$ boys and $3$ girls such that all the girls are not together, is:
questions.sol:
All arrangements: $7!=5040$.
All three girls together: treat them as one unit, $5!\times3!=720$.
Required: $5040-720=4320$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: Let the smallest value of $k\in\mathbb{N}$, for which the coefficient of $x^3$ in $$(1+x)^3+(1+x)^4+(1+x)^5+\ldots+(1+x)^{99}+(1+kx)^{100},\ x\neq0,$$ is $\left(43n+\dfrac{101}{4}\right)\left({}^{100}C_3\right)$ for some $n\in\mathbb{N}$, be $p$. Then the value of $p+n$ is:
questions.sol:
Coefficient of $x^3$: $\sum_{r=3}^{99}{}^rC_3+k^3\,{}^{100}C_3={}^{100}C_4+k^3\,{}^{100}C_3$ (hockey-stick identity).
${}^{100}C_4=\dfrac{97}{4}\,{}^{100}C_3$, so the coefficient is $\left(k^3+\dfrac{97}{4}\right){}^{100}C_3$.
Equating: $k^3+\dfrac{97}{4}=43n+\dfrac{101}{4} \Rightarrow k^3=43n+1$.
$k=1$ gives $n=0\notin\mathbb N$; $k=2,3,4,5$ give $k^3-1=7,26,63,124$, none divisible by $43$.
$k=6$: $215=43\times5$, so $p=6$, $n=5$ and $p+n=11$.

questions.text: Suppose that the mean and median of the non-negative numbers $21, 8, 17, a, 51, 103, b, 13, 67$, $(a>b)$, are $40$ and $21$, respectively. If the mean deviation about the median is $26$, then $2a$ is equal to:
questions.sol:
Mean $40$ with $9$ numbers: sum $=360$, so $a+b=360-280=80$.
Mean deviation about the median $21$ is $26$: $\sum|x_i-21|=234$.
Known numbers give $0+13+4+30+82+8+46=183$, so $|a-21|+|b-21|=51$.
Median is $21$ with $a>b$, so take $b\le21\le a$: $a-b=51$.
With $a+b=80$: $a=65.5$, $b=14.5$ (sorted list $8,13,14.5,17,21,51,65.5,67,103$ has median $21$).
$2a=131$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: Let the line $L_1: x+3=0$ intersect the lines $L_2: x-y=0$ and $L_3: 3x+y=0$ at the points $A$ and $B$, respectively. Let the bisector of the obtuse angle between the lines $L_2$ and $L_3$ intersect the line $L_1$ at the point $C$. Then $BC^2:AC^2$ is equal to:
questions.sol:
$L_2$ and $L_3$ meet at the origin $O$. $A=(-3,-3)$, $B=(-3,9)$.
$\overrightarrow{OA}\cdot\overrightarrow{OB}=9-27<0$, so $\angle AOB$ is the obtuse angle between $L_2$ and $L_3$, and its bisector meets $AB$ (on $L_1$) at $C$.
By the angle bisector theorem, $\dfrac{BC}{AC}=\dfrac{OB}{OA}=\dfrac{\sqrt{90}}{\sqrt{18}}=\sqrt5$.
So $BC^2:AC^2=5:1$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: Let the vertex $A$ of a triangle $ABC$ be $(1,2)$, and the mid-point of the side $AB$ be $(5,-1)$. If the centroid of this triangle is $(3,4)$ and its circumcenter is $(\alpha,\beta)$, then $21(\alpha+\beta)$ is equal to:
questions.sol:
$B=(2\cdot5-1,\ 2(-1)-2)=(9,-4)$; centroid $(3,4)$ gives $C=(9-1-9,\ 12-2+4)=(-1,14)$.
Circumcentre $(x,y)$ equidistant from $A$ and $B$: $4x-3y=23$.
Equidistant from $A$ and $C$: $-x+6y=48$.
Solving: $y=\dfrac{215}{21}$, $x=\dfrac{282}{21}$.
$21(\alpha+\beta)=282+215=497$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: Suppose that two chords, drawn from the point $(1,2)$ on the circle $x^2+y^2+x-3y=0$ are bisected by the $y$-axis. If the other ends of these chords are $R$ and $S$, and the mid point of the line segment $RS$ is $(\alpha,\beta)$, then $6(\alpha+\beta)$ is equal to:
questions.sol:
Let a chord's mid-point be $(0,k)$; its other end is $(-1,\ 2k-2)$.
This point lies on the circle: $1+(2k-2)^2-1-3(2k-2)=0 \Rightarrow (2k-2)(2k-2-3)=0$.
So $2k-2=0$ or $3$: $R=(-1,0)$, $S=(-1,3)$.
Mid-point of $RS$: $\left(-1,\dfrac32\right)$, so $6(\alpha+\beta)=6\cdot\dfrac12=3$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: A line with direction ratios $1,-1,2$ intersects the lines $\dfrac{x}{2}=\dfrac{y}{3}=\dfrac{z+1}{3}$ and $\dfrac{x+1}{-1}=\dfrac{y-2}{1}=\dfrac{z}{4}$ at the points $P$ and $Q$, respectively. If the length of the line segment $PQ$ is $\alpha$, then $225\alpha^2$ is equal to:
questions.sol:
$P=(2s,3s,3s-1)$, $Q=(-1-t,\ 2+t,\ 4t)$, and $\overrightarrow{PQ}=\lambda(1,-1,2)$.
$-1-t-2s=\lambda$ and $2+t-3s=-\lambda$; adding gives $1-5s=0$, so $s=\dfrac15$.
Then $\lambda=-t-\dfrac75$, and $4t-3s+1=2\lambda$ gives $4t+\dfrac25=-2t-\dfrac{14}{5} \Rightarrow t=-\dfrac{8}{15}$, $\lambda=-\dfrac{13}{15}$.
$\alpha=|\lambda|\sqrt6$, so $\alpha^2=\dfrac{169\times6}{225}$ and $225\alpha^2=1014$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: The square of the distance of the point $(-2,-8,6)$ from the line $\dfrac{x-1}{1}=\dfrac{y-1}{2}=\dfrac{z}{-1}$ along the line $\dfrac{x+5}{1}=\dfrac{y+5}{-1}=\dfrac{z}{2}$ is equal to:
questions.sol:
Move from $(-2,-8,6)$ along direction $(1,-1,2)$: point $(-2+t,\ -8-t,\ 6+2t)$.
It lies on the first line when $t-3=\dfrac{-9-t}{2}=-6-2t$, giving $t=-1$ (point $(-3,-7,4)$).
Distance$^2=t^2(1+1+4)=6$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: If $y=\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{3\cos x-4\sin x}{4\cos x+3\sin x}\right)+2\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{x}{1+\sqrt{1-x^2}}\right)$, then $\dfrac{dy}{dx}$ at $x=\dfrac{\sqrt3}{2}$ is equal to:
questions.sol:
Divide by $4\cos x$: $\dfrac{\frac34-\tan x}{1+\frac34\tan x}=\tan(\theta-x)$ with $\tan\theta=\dfrac34$; near $x=\dfrac{\sqrt3}{2}$, $\theta-x\in\left(-\dfrac\pi2,\dfrac\pi2\right)$, so the first term is $\theta-x$, derivative $-1$.
Put $x=\sin\phi$: $\dfrac{\sin\phi}{1+\cos\phi}=\tan\dfrac\phi2$, so the second term is $\phi=\sin^{-1}x$, derivative $\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{1-x^2}}$.
At $x=\dfrac{\sqrt3}{2}$: $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=-1+\dfrac{1}{1/2}=1$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: Let $f$ be a real polynomial of degree $n$ such that $f(x)=f'(x)f''(x)$, for all $x\in\mathbb{R}$. If $f(0)=0$, then $36\left(f'(2)+f''(2)+\int_0^2 f(x)\,dx\right)$ is equal to:
questions.sol:
Degrees: $n=(n-1)+(n-2) \Rightarrow n=3$. Let $f=ax^3+bx^2+cx$ (as $f(0)=0$).
$f'f''=(3ax^2+2bx+c)(6ax+2b)=18a^2x^3+18abx^2+(4b^2+6ac)x+2bc$.
Comparing: $a=18a^2 \Rightarrow a=\dfrac1{18}$; $c=4b^2+\dfrac c3 \Rightarrow c=6b^2$; $2bc=0 \Rightarrow b=c=0$.
$f(x)=\dfrac{x^3}{18}$: $f'(2)=\dfrac23$, $f''(2)=\dfrac23$, $\int_0^2 f=\dfrac{16}{72}=\dfrac29$.
$36\left(\dfrac43+\dfrac29\right)=36\cdot\dfrac{14}{9}=56$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: The area of the region $\{(x,y): y\le\pi-|x|,\ y\le|x\sin x|,\ y\ge0\}$ is:
questions.sol:
The region is symmetric about the $y$-axis and needs $|x|\le\pi$. For $0\le x\le\pi$, $x\sin x\ge0$.
$x\sin x=\pi-x$ at $x=\dfrac\pi2$; $x\sin x$ is the lower curve on $\left[0,\dfrac\pi2\right]$ and $\pi-x$ on $\left[\dfrac\pi2,\pi\right]$.
Right half: $\int_0^{\pi/2}x\sin x\,dx+\int_{\pi/2}^{\pi}(\pi-x)\,dx=\left[\sin x-x\cos x\right]_0^{\pi/2}+\dfrac{\pi^2}{8}=1+\dfrac{\pi^2}{8}$.
Total area $=2\left(1+\dfrac{\pi^2}{8}\right)=2+\dfrac{\pi^2}{4}$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: Let $\displaystyle\int_{-2}^{2}\left(|\sin x|+[x\sin x]\right)dx=2(3-\cos2)+\beta$, where $[\cdot]$ is the greatest integer function. Then $\beta\sin\left(\dfrac{\beta}{2}\right)$ equals:
questions.sol:
$\int_{-2}^{2}|\sin x|\,dx=2\int_0^2\sin x\,dx=2(1-\cos2)$.
$x\sin x$ is even, increasing on $[0,2]$ from $0$ to $2\sin2\approx1.82$. Let $x_0\in(0,2)$ with $x_0\sin x_0=1$.
So $[x\sin x]=1$ for $x_0\le|x|\le2$ and $0$ otherwise: $\int_{-2}^{2}[x\sin x]\,dx=2(2-x_0)$.
Total $=2(3-\cos2)-2x_0$, so $\beta=-2x_0$.
$\beta\sin\dfrac\beta2=(-2x_0)\sin(-x_0)=2x_0\sin x_0=2$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: Let $y=y(x)$ be the solution of the differential equation $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=(1+x+x^2)(1-y+y^2)$, $y(0)=\dfrac12$. Then $(2y(1)-1)$ is equal to
questions.sol:
Separate: $\dfrac{dy}{\left(y-\frac12\right)^2+\frac34}=(1+x+x^2)\,dx$.
Integrate: $\dfrac{2}{\sqrt3}\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{2y-1}{\sqrt3}\right)=x+\dfrac{x^2}{2}+\dfrac{x^3}{3}+c$, and $y(0)=\dfrac12$ gives $c=0$.
At $x=1$: $\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{2y-1}{\sqrt3}\right)=\dfrac{\sqrt3}{2}\cdot\dfrac{11}{6}=\dfrac{11\sqrt3}{12}$.
So $2y(1)-1=\sqrt3\tan\left(\dfrac{11\sqrt3}{12}\right)$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: A coin is tossed $8$ times. If the probability that exactly $4$ heads appear in the first six tosses and exactly $3$ heads appear in the last five tosses is $p$, then $96p$ is equal to ______.
questions.sol:
First six tosses: 1–6; last five: 4–8. Tosses 4, 5, 6 are common. Let $k$ heads fall in tosses 4–6.
Then tosses 1–3 have $4-k$ heads and tosses 7–8 have $3-k$ heads, so $1\le k\le3$.
Count $=\sum_k\binom3k\binom3{4-k}\binom2{3-k}$: $k=1$: $3\cdot1\cdot1=3$; $k=2$: $3\cdot3\cdot2=18$; $k=3$: $1\cdot3\cdot1=3$. Total $24$.
$p=\dfrac{24}{2^8}=\dfrac{3}{32}$, so $96p=9$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: Consider the parabola $P: y^2=4kx$ and the ellipse $E: \dfrac{x^2}{a^2}+\dfrac{y^2}{b^2}=1$. Let the line segment joining the points of intersection of $P$ and $E$, be their latus rectums. If the eccentricity of $E$ is $e$, then $e^2+2\sqrt2$ is equal to ______.
questions.sol:
The common latus rectum is $x=k$ for $P$ (ends $(k,\pm2k)$) and $x=ae$ for $E$ (ends $\left(ae,\pm\dfrac{b^2}{a}\right)$).
So $ae=k$ and $\dfrac{b^2}{a}=2k=2ae \Rightarrow b^2=2a^2e$.
$b^2=a^2(1-e^2) \Rightarrow 1-e^2=2e \Rightarrow e^2+2e-1=0 \Rightarrow e=\sqrt2-1$.
$e^2=3-2\sqrt2$, so $e^2+2\sqrt2=3$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: If $A=\dfrac{\sin3^\circ}{\cos9^\circ}+\dfrac{\sin9^\circ}{\cos27^\circ}+\dfrac{\sin27^\circ}{\cos81^\circ}$ and $B=\tan81^\circ-\tan3^\circ$, then $\dfrac{B}{A}$ is equal to ______.
questions.sol:
$\tan3\theta-\tan\theta=\dfrac{\sin2\theta}{\cos3\theta\cos\theta}=\dfrac{2\sin\theta}{\cos3\theta}$, so $\dfrac{\sin\theta}{\cos3\theta}=\dfrac12(\tan3\theta-\tan\theta)$.
$A=\dfrac12\left[(\tan9^\circ-\tan3^\circ)+(\tan27^\circ-\tan9^\circ)+(\tan81^\circ-\tan27^\circ)\right]=\dfrac12(\tan81^\circ-\tan3^\circ)=\dfrac B2$.
$\dfrac BA=2$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: Let $\vec{a}_k=(\tan\theta_k)\hat{i}+\hat{j}$ and $\vec{b}_k=\hat{i}-(\cot\theta_k)\hat{j}$, where $\theta_k=\dfrac{2^{k-1}\pi}{2^n+1}$, for some $n\in\mathbb{N}$, $n>5$. Then the value of $\dfrac{\sum_{k=1}^{n}|\vec{a}_k|^2}{\sum_{k=1}^{n}|\vec{b}_k|^2}$ is ______.
questions.sol:
$|\vec a_k|^2=1+\tan^2\theta_k=\sec^2\theta_k$ and $|\vec b_k|^2=1+\cot^2\theta_k=\csc^2\theta_k$. Let $S=\sum_{k=1}^n\csc^2\theta_k$.
$\sec^2\theta+\csc^2\theta=\dfrac{1}{\sin^2\theta\cos^2\theta}=4\csc^2 2\theta$, so $\sec^2\theta_k=4\csc^2\theta_{k+1}-\csc^2\theta_k$.
$\theta_{n+1}=\dfrac{2^n\pi}{2^n+1}=\pi-\theta_1$, so $\csc^2\theta_{n+1}=\csc^2\theta_1$ and $\sum_{k=1}^n\csc^2\theta_{k+1}=S$.
$\sum\sec^2\theta_k=4S-S=3S$, so the ratio is $3$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: The number of points, at which the function $f(x)=\max\{6x,\ 2+3x^2\}+|x-1|\cos\left|x^2-\dfrac14\right|$, $x\in(-\pi,\pi)$, is not differentiable, is ______.
questions.sol:
$\max\{6x,2+3x^2\}$: $3x^2-6x+2=0$ at $x=1\pm\dfrac{1}{\sqrt3}$ (both in $(-\pi,\pi)$). The slopes there are $6$ and $6x\neq6$, so there are $2$ corners.
$\cos\left|x^2-\dfrac14\right|=\cos\left(x^2-\dfrac14\right)$ is smooth, and $|x-1|\cos\left(x^2-\dfrac14\right)$ has a corner at $x=1$ since $\cos\dfrac34\neq0$.
At $x=1$ the max part ($=6x$) is smooth. Total: $3$ points.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: In a screw gauge when the circular scale is given five complete rotations it moves linearly by $2.5$ mm. If the circular scale has $100$ divisions, the least count of screw gauge is _________ mm.
questions.sol:
Pitch $=\dfrac{2.5}{5}=0.5$ mm.
Least count $=\dfrac{\text{pitch}}{\text{number of divisions}}=\dfrac{0.5}{100}=5\times10^{-3}$ mm.

questions.text:
The increase in the pressure required to decrease the volume $(\Delta V)$ of water is $6.3\times10^7\ \mathrm{N/m^2}$. The percentage decrease in the volume is _______.
(Bulk modulus of water $=2.1\times10^9\ \mathrm{N/m^2}$.)
questions.sol:
$B=\dfrac{\Delta p}{\Delta V/V} \Rightarrow \dfrac{\Delta V}{V}=\dfrac{6.3\times10^7}{2.1\times10^9}=0.03$.
Percentage decrease $=3\%$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: The time taken by a block of mass $m$ to slide down from the highest point to the lowest point on a rough inclined plane is $50\,\%$ more compared to the time taken by the same block on identical inclined smooth plane. Both inclined planes are at $45^\circ$ with the horizontal. The coefficient of kinetic friction between the rough inclined surface and block is _______.
questions.sol:
Same length $L=\dfrac12at^2$, so $a\propto\dfrac1{t^2}$: $\dfrac{a_{\text{smooth}}}{a_{\text{rough}}}=(1.5)^2=\dfrac94$.
At $45^\circ$: $a_{\text{smooth}}=g\sin45^\circ$, $a_{\text{rough}}=g\sin45^\circ(1-\mu)$.
$\dfrac{1}{1-\mu}=\dfrac94 \Rightarrow \mu=1-\dfrac49=\dfrac59$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: Two nuclei of mass number $3$ combine with another nucleus of mass number $4$ to yield a nucleus of mass number $10$. If the binding energy per nucleon for the mass numbers $3$, $4$ and $10$ are $5.6$ MeV, $7.4$ MeV and $6.1$ MeV, respectively, then in the process, $\Delta Mc^2=$ ______ MeV.
questions.sol:
Binding energy of the reactants: $2\times3\times5.6+4\times7.4=33.6+29.6=63.2$ MeV.
Binding energy of the product: $10\times6.1=61$ MeV.
The product is less tightly bound, so the mass increases: $\Delta Mc^2=63.2-61=2.2$ MeV.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: A solid sphere of mass $M$ and radius $R$ is divided into two unequal parts. The smaller part having mass $M/8$ is converted into a sphere of radius $r$ and the larger part is converted into a circular disc of thickness $t$ and radius $2R$. If $I_1$ is moment of inertia of a sphere having radius $r$ about an axis through its centre and $I_2$ is the moment of inertia of a disc about its diameter, the ratio of their moment of inertia $I_2/I_1=$ _____.
questions.sol:
Same density: mass $\dfrac M8$ means volume $\dfrac18$, so $r=\dfrac R2$.
$I_1=\dfrac25\cdot\dfrac M8\cdot\dfrac{R^2}{4}=\dfrac{MR^2}{80}$.
Disc of mass $\dfrac{7M}{8}$, radius $2R$ (thin), about a diameter: $I_2=\dfrac14\cdot\dfrac{7M}{8}(2R)^2=\dfrac{7MR^2}{8}$.
$\dfrac{I_2}{I_1}=\dfrac78\times80=70$.

questions.text: The graph shows variation of stopping potential $V_0$ with the frequency $\nu$ of the incident radiation for three photosensitive metals $X_1$, $X_2$ and $X_3$. Which metal will give out electrons with greater kinetic energy, for the same wavelength of incident radiation?
options: All the metals will give out photo electrons with same kinetic energies.
questions.sol:
$eV_0=K_{\max}=h u-h u_0$: the lines are parallel and the threshold frequency is where each meets the $ u$-axis.
$X_1$ has the lowest threshold ($1.0 imes10^{14}$ Hz), i.e. the smallest work function.
For the same incident frequency, $K_{\max}$ is greatest for $X_1$.

questions.text: A slit of width $a$ is illuminated by light of wavelength $\lambda$. The linear separation between $1^{\text{st}}$ and $3^{\text{rd}}$ minima in the diffraction pattern produced on a screen placed at a distance $D$ from the slit system is ________.
questions.sol:
Single-slit minima: $a\sin\theta=n\lambda$, so $y_n=\dfrac{nD\lambda}{a}$.
$y_3-y_1=\dfrac{2D\lambda}{a}$.

questions.text:
A string $A$ of length $0.314$ m and Young's modulus $2\times10^{10}\ \mathrm{N/m^2}$ is connected to another string $B$ of length and Young's modulus both twice of those of $A$. This series combination of strings is then suspended from a rigid support and its free end is fixed to a load of mass $0.8$ kg. The net change in length of the combination is ________ mm.
(radius of both the strings is $0.2$ mm and acceleration due to gravity $=10\ \mathrm{m/s^2}$)
(Mass of both strings is to be neglected as compared to the mass of load)
questions.sol:
Tension $F=0.8\times10=8$ N in both strings; area $A=\pi(0.2\times10^{-3})^2=1.256\times10^{-7}\ \mathrm{m^2}$.
$\Delta L_A=\dfrac{FL}{AY}=\dfrac{8\times0.314}{1.256\times10^{-7}\times2\times10^{10}}=1\times10^{-3}$ m $=1$ mm.
For $B$, $L$ and $Y$ are both doubled, so $\Delta L_B=\Delta L_A=1$ mm.
Net change $=2$ mm.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: One gas of $n_1$ mole of molecules at temperature $T_1$, volume $V_1$, and pressure $P_1$, and another gas of $n_2$ mole of molecules at temperature $T_2$, volume $V_2$, and pressure $P_2$, are mixed resulting in pressure $P$ and volume $V$ of the mixture. The temperature of the mixture is _________.
questions.sol:
$n_1=\dfrac{P_1V_1}{RT_1}$, $n_2=\dfrac{P_2V_2}{RT_2}$, and the mixture obeys $PV=(n_1+n_2)RT$.
$T=\dfrac{PV}{(n_1+n_2)R}=\dfrac{PV}{\dfrac{P_1V_1}{T_1}+\dfrac{P_2V_2}{T_2}}=\dfrac{T_1T_2PV}{T_2P_1V_1+T_1P_2V_2}$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text:
An ideal gas undergoes a process maintaining relation between pressure $(P)$ and volume $(V)$ as $P=P_0\left(1+\left(\dfrac{V_0}{V}\right)^2\right)^{-1}$, where $P_0$ and $V_0$ are constants. If two samples $A$ and $B$ (two moles each) with initial volumes $V_0$ and $3V_0$ respectively undergo above mentioned process and attain same pressure, then the difference at the temperatures of these samples, $T_B-T_A$ is __________.
($R=$ gas constant)
questions.note: Dropped in the official final key: full marks to everyone.
questions.sol:
Both samples follow the same $P$–$V$ relation, so at the same pressure they would have the same volume and the same temperature; the question as worded is ambiguous.
The intended reading compares the two initial states, with $T=\dfrac{PV}{nR}$, $n=2$:
$A$: $V=V_0$, $P=\dfrac{P_0}{2}$, $T_A=\dfrac{P_0V_0}{4R}$.
$B$: $V=3V_0$, $P=\dfrac{P_0}{1+\frac19}=\dfrac{9P_0}{10}$, $T_B=\dfrac{27P_0V_0}{20R}$.
$T_B-T_A=\dfrac{27-5}{20}\cdot\dfrac{P_0V_0}{R}=\dfrac{11P_0V_0}{10R}$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: A voltmeter with internal resistance of $x\ \Omega$ can be used to measure upto $20$ V. In order to increase its measuring range to $30$ V, the required modification is to____________.
options: connect resistor of $\dfrac{x}{2}\ \Omega$, in series with voltmeter.
connect resistor of $\dfrac{x}{2}\ \Omega$, in parallel to voltmeter.
connect a resistor of $x\ \Omega$ in series with voltmeter.
connect resistor of $2x\ \Omega$ in parallel to voltmeter.
questions.sol:
Full-scale current $I=\dfrac{20}{x}$.
For $30$ V the total resistance must be $\dfrac{30}{I}=1.5x$, so a resistance of $0.5x=\dfrac x2\ \Omega$ is added in series.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: Two 4 bits binary numbers, $A=1101$ and $B=1010$ are given in the inputs of a logic circuit shown in figure below. The output $(Y)$ will be :
questions.sol:
The circuit gives $Y=\overline{\bar A\cdot B}$ (NOT on $A$, then NAND with $B$).
$\bar A=0010$; $\bar A\cdot B=0010\cdot1010=0010$ (bitwise).
$Y=\overline{0010}=1101$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: A rod of length $10$ cm lies along the principle axis of a concave mirror of focal length $10$ cm as shown in figure. The length of the image is ________ cm.
questions.sol:
The near end is at $20$ cm $=2f$ (centre of curvature), so its image is also at $20$ cm.
Far end: $u=-30$ cm, $f=-10$ cm: $\dfrac1v=\dfrac1f-\dfrac1u=-\dfrac1{10}+\dfrac1{30}=-\dfrac1{15}$, so $v=-15$ cm.
Image length $=20-15=5$ cm.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: A parallel plate air capacitor is connected to a battery. The plates are pulled apart at uniform speed $v$. If $x$ is the separation between the plates at any instant, then the time rate of change of electrostatic energy of the capacitor is proportional to $x^\alpha$, where $\alpha$ is _______.
questions.sol:
$V$ is constant: $U=\dfrac12CV^2=\dfrac{\epsilon_0AV^2}{2x}$.
$\dfrac{dU}{dt}=-\dfrac{\epsilon_0AV^2}{2x^2}\dfrac{dx}{dt}=-\dfrac{\epsilon_0AV^2v}{2x^2}\propto x^{-2}$.
$\alpha=-2$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: An insulated wire is wound so that it forms a flat coil with $N=200$ turns. The radius of the innermost turn is $r_1=3$ cm, and of the outermost turn $r_2=6$ cm. If $20$ mA current flows in it then the magnetic moment will be $\alpha\times10^{-2}\ \mathrm{A\,m^2}$. The value of $\alpha$ is_____.
questions.sol:
Turns per unit radial width: $\dfrac{N}{r_2-r_1}$. A ring of width $dr$ has $\dfrac{N\,dr}{r_2-r_1}$ turns of area $\pi r^2$.
$m=\int_{r_1}^{r_2}\dfrac{NI\pi r^2}{r_2-r_1}dr=\dfrac{NI\pi(r_2^3-r_1^3)}{3(r_2-r_1)}$.
$=\dfrac{200\times0.02\times\pi\times(216-27)\times10^{-6}}{3\times0.03}=4\pi\times2.1\times10^{-3}\approx2.64\times10^{-2}\ \mathrm{A\,m^2}$.
$\alpha=2.64$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: Consider a circuit consisting of a capacitor ($20\ \mu$F), resistor ($100\ \Omega$) and two identical diodes as shown in figure. The resistance of diode under forward biasing condition is $10\ \Omega$. The time constant of the circuit is $\alpha\times10^{-3}$ s. The value of $\alpha$ is __________
questions.sol:
The two diodes are connected in antiparallel, so for either direction of current exactly one is forward biased ($10\ \Omega$) and the other is off.
Total resistance $=100+10=110\ \Omega$.
$\tau=RC=110\times20\times10^{-6}=2.2\times10^{-3}$ s, so $\alpha=2.2$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: The voltage and the current between $A$ and $B$ points shown in the circuit are____________.
questions.sol:
Between $A$ and $B$ there are four identical source branches ($27$ V with $3\ \Omega$; the third has $14+13=27$ V) and one load branch of $3+3=6\ \Omega$.
The four sources in parallel are equivalent to $27$ V with internal resistance $\dfrac34\ \Omega$.
$I=\dfrac{27}{6+0.75}=4$ A through the $6\ \Omega$ branch, and $V_{AB}=4\times6=24$ V.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: A telescope with objective diameter $R$ is used to observe a distant star emitting light of wavelength $500$ nm, at a resolution of $5\times10^{-7}$ radian. The value of $R$ is _________ cm.
questions.sol:
Limit of resolution $\theta=\dfrac{1.22\lambda}{D}$.
$D=\dfrac{1.22\times500\times10^{-9}}{5\times10^{-7}}=1.22$ m $=122$ cm.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: An unpolarized light is incident on the plane interface of air-dielectric medium shown in figure. If the incident angle is equal to Brewster angle, identify the expression representing reflected wave.
questions.sol:
The interface is the $xy$-plane and the medium is on the $+z$ side; the plane of incidence is the $xz$-plane.
The incident wave travels along $+x$ and $+z$; the reflected wave keeps its $x$-component and reverses its $z$-component, so its phase is $(kx-kz-\omega t)$, with no $y$-dependence.
Only option (A) has this phase. At the Brewster angle the reflected light is plane polarised perpendicular to the plane of incidence (along $\hat j$).
Official answer: (A).
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: A $1$ kg block subjected to two simultaneous forces $(2\hat{i}+3\hat{j}+4\hat{k})$ N and $(3\hat{i}-\hat{j}-2\hat{k})$ N is moved a distance of $25$ m along $(3\hat{i}-4\hat{j})$ direction. The work done in this process is ________ J.
questions.sol:
Net force $\vec F=5\hat i+2\hat j+2\hat k$ N.
Displacement $\vec d=25\cdot\dfrac{3\hat i-4\hat j}{5}=15\hat i-20\hat j$ m.
$W=\vec F\cdot\vec d=75-40=35$ J.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text:
The surface tension of a soap solution is $3.5\times10^{-2}$ N/m. The work required to increase the radius of a soap bubble from $1$ cm to $2$ cm is $\alpha\times10^{-6}$ J. The value of $\alpha$ is ________.
($\pi=22/7$)
questions.sol:
A soap bubble has two surfaces: $W=T\times2\times4\pi(r_2^2-r_1^2)$.
$W=3.5\times10^{-2}\times8\times\dfrac{22}{7}\times(4-1)\times10^{-4}=0.88\times3\times10^{-4}=264\times10^{-6}$ J.
$\alpha=264$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: The velocity of a particle executing simple harmonic motion along $x$-axis is described as $v^2=50-x^2$, where $x$ represents displacement. If the time period of motion is $\dfrac{x}{7}$ s, the value of $x$ is ________.
questions.sol:
In SHM $v^2=\omega^2(A^2-x^2)$; comparing, $\omega^2=1$, so $\omega=1$ rad/s.
$T=\dfrac{2\pi}{\omega}=2\pi=2\times\dfrac{22}{7}=\dfrac{44}{7}$ s.
So $x=44$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: A body of mass $2$ kg begins to move under the influence of time dependent force $\vec{F}=(2t\hat{i}+6t^2\hat{j})$ N, where $\hat{i}$ and $\hat{j}$ are unit vectors along $x$ and $y$-axis respectively. The power produced by the force at $t=2$ s is ____ W.
questions.sol:
$\vec a=\dfrac{\vec F}{m}=t\hat i+3t^2\hat j$; starting from rest, $\vec v=\dfrac{t^2}{2}\hat i+t^3\hat j$.
At $t=2$ s: $\vec F=4\hat i+24\hat j$ N, $\vec v=2\hat i+8\hat j$ m/s.
$P=\vec F\cdot\vec v=8+192=200$ W.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: An inductor of $10$ mH, capacitor of $0.1\ \mu$F and a resistor of $100\ \Omega$ are connected in series across an a.c power supply $220$ V, $70$ Hz. The power factor of the given circuit is $0.5$. The difference in the inductive reactance and capacitance reactance is $\sqrt3\,\alpha\ \Omega$. The value of $\alpha$ is ________.
questions.sol:
$\cos\phi=0.5 \Rightarrow \phi=60^\circ$, and $\tan\phi=\dfrac{|X_L-X_C|}{R}=\sqrt3$.
$|X_L-X_C|=\sqrt3\times100\ \Omega$, so $\alpha=100$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: Number of moles and number of molecules in $1.4187$ L of $\mathrm{SO_2}$ at STP respectively are
questions.sol:
At STP one mole of gas occupies $22.414$ L: $n=\dfrac{1.4187}{22.414}=0.0633$ mol.
Molecules $=0.0633\times6.022\times10^{23}=3.812\times10^{22}$.

questions.text: What is the ratio of wave number of first line (lowest energy line) of Balmer series of H atomic spectrum to first line of its Brackett series?
questions.sol:
Balmer, first line ($3\to2$): $\bar\nu=R\left(\dfrac14-\dfrac19\right)=\dfrac{5R}{36}$.
Brackett, first line ($5\to4$): $\bar\nu=R\left(\dfrac1{16}-\dfrac1{25}\right)=\dfrac{9R}{400}$.
Ratio $=\dfrac{5}{36}\cdot\dfrac{400}{9}=\dfrac{2000}{324}\approx6.17=5:0.81$.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: Which of the following is correct set of $4$ quantum numbers of $19^{\text{th}}$ electron in Chromium (Atomic number $=24$) in accordance with Aufbau principle?
questions.sol:
Aufbau order: $1s^2\,2s^2\,2p^6\,3s^2\,3p^6$ accounts for $18$ electrons; the $19^{\text{th}}$ enters $4s$ (lower $n+l$ than $3d$).
For $4s$: $n=4$, $l=0$, $m=0$, $s=+\dfrac12$.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: For an ideal gas, heat capacity at constant volume is always greater than the heat capacity at constant pressure.
Statement II: In a constant volume process, no work is produced and all the heat withdrawn goes into the chaotic motion and is reflected by a temperature increase of the ideal gas.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.sol:
For an ideal gas $C_p-C_v=R>0$, so $C_v$ is smaller: Statement I is false.
At constant volume $w=0$, so $q_V=\Delta U$: all the heat goes into the random (chaotic) motion of the molecules, seen as a rise in temperature. Statement II is true.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: At $T$(K), the equilibrium constant of $\mathrm{A_2(g)+B_2(g)\rightleftharpoons C(g)}$ is $2.7\times10^{-5}$. What is the equilibrium constant for $\dfrac13\mathrm{A_2(g)}+\dfrac13\mathrm{B_2(g)}\rightleftharpoons\dfrac13\mathrm{C(g)}$ at the same temperature?
questions.sol:
Multiplying an equation by $\dfrac13$ raises $K$ to the power $\dfrac13$.
$K'=(2.7\times10^{-5})^{1/3}=(27\times10^{-6})^{1/3}=3\times10^{-2}$.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: In order to oxidise a mixture of $1$ mole each of $\mathrm{FeC_2O_4}$, $\mathrm{Fe_2(C_2O_4)_3}$, $\mathrm{FeSO_4}$ and $\mathrm{Fe_2(SO_4)_3}$ in acidic medium, the number of moles of $\mathrm{KMnO_4}$ required is
questions.sol:
Electrons released: $\mathrm{Fe^{2+}\to Fe^{3+}}$ gives $1$; each $\mathrm{C_2O_4^{2-}\to 2CO_2}$ gives $2$.
$\mathrm{FeC_2O_4}$: $1+2=3$; $\mathrm{Fe_2(C_2O_4)_3}$: $3\times2=6$; $\mathrm{FeSO_4}$: $1$; $\mathrm{Fe_2(SO_4)_3}$: $0$. Total $10$ mol electrons.
$\mathrm{MnO_4^-\to Mn^{2+}}$ takes $5$ electrons, so $\dfrac{10}{5}=2$ mol $\mathrm{KMnO_4}$.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Consider the first order reaction $\mathrm{R\to P}$.
The fraction of molecules decomposed in the given first order reaction can be expressed as
questions.sol:
First order: $[\mathrm R]=[\mathrm R]_0e^{-k_1t}$.
Fraction decomposed $=\dfrac{[\mathrm R]_0-[\mathrm R]}{[\mathrm R]_0}=1-e^{-k_1t}$.

questions.text: A monoatomic anion $(\mathrm{A^-})$ has $45$ neutrons and $36$ electrons. Atomic mass, group in the periodic table and physical state at room temperature of the element (A) respectively are
questions.sol:
$\mathrm{A^-}$ has $36$ electrons, so $Z=35$: bromine.
Mass number $=35+45=80$; bromine is in group $17$ and is a liquid at room temperature.

questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

questions.text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: The covalency of oxygen is generally two but it can exceed upto four. The oxidation state of oxygen in $\mathrm{SO_2}$ is $-2$ and in $\mathrm{OF_2}$ it is $+2$.
Statement II: The anomalous behaviour of oxygen when compared to the other elements of group $16$ is due to its small size and high electronegativity.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.sol:
Oxygen has no $d$ orbitals, so its covalency is usually two and at most four. In $\mathrm{SO_2}$ it is $-2$; in $\mathrm{OF_2}$, F is more electronegative, so O is $+2$. Statement I is true.
Oxygen's anomalous behaviour arises from its small size, high electronegativity (and absence of $d$ orbitals). Statement II is true.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
The correct statements among the following are,
A. Mo(VI) and W(VI) are less stable than Cr(VI).
B. $\mathrm{Ce^{4+}}$ and $\mathrm{Tb^{4+}}$ are oxidant while $\mathrm{Eu^{2+}}$ and $\mathrm{Yb^{2+}}$ are reductant.
C. Cm and Am have seven unpaired electrons.
D. Actinoid contraction is greater from element to element than lanthanoid contraction.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.sol:
A: false. Higher oxidation states become more stable down a group, so Mo(VI) and W(VI) are more stable than Cr(VI).
B: true. $\mathrm{Ce^{4+}}$, $\mathrm{Tb^{4+}}$ tend to return to $+3$ (oxidants); $\mathrm{Eu^{2+}}$, $\mathrm{Yb^{2+}}$ tend to go to $+3$ (reductants).
C: false. Am ($5f^7 7s^2$) has $7$ unpaired electrons but Cm ($5f^7 6d^1 7s^2$) has $8$.
D: true. Poor shielding by $5f$ electrons makes the actinoid contraction greater from element to element.
B and D only.

questions.text:
Correct statements from the following are
A. Potassium dichromate is an oxidising agent and it oxidises $\mathrm{FeSO_4}$ to $\mathrm{Fe_2(SO_4)_3}$ in acidic medium.
B. Sodium dichromate can be used as primary standard in volumetric estimation.
C. $\mathrm{CrO_4^{2-}}$ and $\mathrm{Cr_2O_7^{2-}}$ are interconvertible in aqueous solution by varying the pH of the solution.
D. Cr-O-Cr bond angle in $\mathrm{Cr_2O_7^{2-}}$ is $126^\circ$.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.sol:
A: true. $\mathrm{Cr_2O_7^{2-}+14H^++6Fe^{2+}\to2Cr^{3+}+6Fe^{3+}+7H_2O}$.
B: false. Sodium dichromate is hygroscopic; potassium dichromate is the primary standard.
C: true. $\mathrm{2CrO_4^{2-}+2H^+\rightleftharpoons Cr_2O_7^{2-}+H_2O}$ shifts with pH.
D: true. The Cr–O–Cr angle in dichromate is $126^\circ$.
A, C and D only.

Increasing order of electron withdrawing power of following functional groups is:

questions.text:
An alkene (X) on ozonolysis followed by reduction gives following products.
$\mathrm{H{-}CO{-}H}$ (2 moles), $\mathrm{H{-}CO{-}CO{-}CO{-}H}$, $\mathrm{CH_3{-}CO{-}CO{-}CO{-}CH_3}$
The alkene (X) is:
questions.sol:
Products contain $2+3+5=10$ C. Two HCHO come from two exocyclic $=\mathrm{CH_2}$ groups; the other two products come from a six-membered ring cut at two ring C=C bonds.
$\mathrm{OHC{-}CO{-}CHO}$: a three-carbon ring segment $\mathrm{CH{=}}$, $\mathrm{C(=CH_2)}$, $\mathrm{{=}CH}$.
$\mathrm{CH_3CO{-}CO{-}COCH_3}$: a three-carbon segment $\mathrm{C(CH_3){=}}$, $\mathrm{C(=CH_2)}$, $\mathrm{{=}C(CH_3)}$.
So X is a cyclohexadiene with two ring C=C bonds, two exocyclic $=\mathrm{CH_2}$ groups and two methyl groups, one on each side of the same exocyclic carbon; this is the structure in option (D).

questions.text: Amongst the following, the total number of compounds soluble in aqueous NaOH at room temperature is:

questions.text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: The structure of Maltose is given below (structure (I) in the figure). Maltose is a non-reducing sugar.
Statement II: The structure of Lactose is given below (structure (II) in the figure). Lactose is a reducing sugar.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.sol:
Maltose has a free hemiacetal (anomeric $-\mathrm{OH}$) on its second glucose unit, which can open to an aldehyde: maltose is a reducing sugar, so Statement I is false.
Lactose ($\beta$-D-galactose C-1 linked to C-4 of D-glucose) keeps a free anomeric $-\mathrm{OH}$ on the glucose unit: it is a reducing sugar. Statement II is true.

questions.text: Identify the colour of compound 'X' in the sequence of the reaction.
questions.sol:
Phenol and phthalic anhydride in conc. $\mathrm{H_2SO_4}$ give phenolphthalein (colourless lactone form).

questions.text: According to Lewis theory, the total number of $\sigma$ bond-pairs and lone pair of electrons around the central atom of $\mathrm{XeO_6^{4-}}$ ion is ________.
questions.sol:
In $\mathrm{XeO_6^{4-}}$ (perxenate), Xe is bonded to six O atoms and uses all eight valence electrons in bonding (oxidation state $+8$).
So there are $6$ $\sigma$ bond pairs and $0$ lone pairs on Xe (octahedral).
Total $=6$.

questions.text:
Consider the following sequence of reactions to give the major product (X)
P g of the major product (X) formed is reacted with $\mathrm{NaHCO_3}$ solution to liberate a gas which occupied $11.2\ \mathrm{dm^3}$ at STP.
$\mathrm{P}=$ ________ g.
(Given molar mass in $\mathrm{g\,mol^{-1}}$ H:1, C:12, O:16, Cl:35.5)

(i) Friedel–Crafts methylation gives toluene. (ii) $\mathrm{Cl_2/FeCl_3}$ chlorinates the ring; the major product is 4-chlorotoluene. (iii) $\mathrm{K_2Cr_2O_7/H_2SO_4}$ oxidises $\mathrm{-CH_3}$ to $\mathrm{-COOH}$: X = 4-chlorobenzoic acid, $\mathrm{C_7H_5ClO_2}$, $M=156.5\ \mathrm{g\,mol^{-1}}$.
$\mathrm{ArCOOH+NaHCO_3\to ArCOONa+CO_2+H_2O}$; $11.2\ \mathrm{dm^3}$ $\mathrm{CO_2}$ at STP $=0.5$ mol, so $0.5$ mol acid.
$\mathrm{P}=0.5\times156.5=78.25\approx78$ g.

questions.text:
$2.0$ g of a bromo hydrocarbon (X) was subjected to Carius analysis, gave $3.36$ g of AgBr. The percentage of carbon in the compound (X) is $26.7\%$. Total number of carbon atoms in the empirical formula for compound (X) is _______.
(Given molar mass in $\mathrm{g\,mol^{-1}}$ H:1, C:12, Br:80, Ag:108)
questions.sol:

questions.text:
The pH of a solution obtained by mixing $5$ mL of $0.1$ M $\mathrm{NH_4OH}$ solution with $250$ mL of $0.1$ M $\mathrm{NH_4Cl}$ solution is _______ $\times10^{-2}$. (Nearest integer)
Given: $\mathrm{p}K_b(\mathrm{NH_4OH})=4.74$
$\log2=0.30$
$\log3=0.48$
$\log5=0.70$
questions.sol:
Basic buffer: base $=0.5$ mmol, salt $=25$ mmol.
$\mathrm{pOH}=\mathrm pK_b+\log\dfrac{[\text{salt}]}{[\text{base}]}=4.74+\log50=4.74+1.70=6.44$.
$\mathrm{pH}=14-6.44=7.56=756\times10^{-2}$.

questions.text:
A non-volatile, non-electrolyte solid solute when dissolved in $40$ g of a solvent, the vapour pressure of the solvent decreased from $760$ mm Hg to $750$ mm Hg. If the same solution boils at $320$ K, then the number of moles of the solvent present in the solution is _______. (Nearest integer)
[Given: boiling point of the pure solvent $=319.5$ K, $K_b$ of the solvent $=0.3\ \mathrm{K\,kg\,mol^{-1}}$]
questions.sol:
$\Delta T_b=0.5=K_bm \Rightarrow m=\dfrac53\ \mathrm{mol\,kg^{-1}}$, so moles of solute $n_2=\dfrac53\times0.040=\dfrac1{15}$.
Relative lowering: $\dfrac{760-750}{760}=\dfrac{1}{76}=\dfrac{n_2}{n_1+n_2}$, so $n_1+n_2=76n_2$, i.e. $n_1=75n_2$.
$n_1=\dfrac{75}{15}=5$.
